summary: Reproduced that CompressedTensorsW4AFP8MoE accepted group_size=64 even though all six CUTLASS W4A8 MoE kernel calls use chunk_size=128. Added an initialization-time rejection for every unsupported group size, preserving group_size=128 behavior and preventing silently mis-scaled checkpoints from loading.

tests.what_was_measured: The actual scheme constructor accepted unsupported group sizes 64, 127, and 256; three rejection assertions failed while the group_size=128 boundary passed. Raw output: reports/j-5efeb1588e4b/raw/regression-before.txt

The supported group_size=128 configuration constructs, while independent unsupported boundaries 64, 127, and 256 raise the explicit safety error; 4 tests passed. Raw output: reports/j-5efeb1588e4b/raw/regression-after.txt
The existing mocked DeepEP W4A8 MoE call-path regression remained passing; 1 test passed. Raw output: reports/j-5efeb1588e4b/raw/related-unit.txt

Platform qualification only: all 605 numerical kernel cases skipped because this CUTLASS implementation requires NVIDIA sm90, while the assigned GPU is AMD gfx950. Raw output: reports/j-5efeb1588e4b/raw/kernel-platform-check.txt
Changed source and regression test compile successfully. Raw output: reports/j-5efeb1588e4b/raw/compileall.txt

gpu_execution_evidence: The assigned device is one AMD Instinct MI350X, gfx950, with Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2. The affected kernel and its tests require NVIDIA Hopper sm90, so no issue-relevant GPU execution was possible. Hardware evidence: reports/j-5efeb1588e4b/raw/hardware.txt
remaining_limitations: No H100/sm90 was available, and no affected W4A8 MoE checkpoint weights were supplied. Therefore full model serving, semantic accuracy, and direct CUTLASS numerical behavior (including the report's K-per-rank observation) remain unverified. The correction intentionally rejects non-128 group sizes rather than claiming kernel support for them. No native source changed, so a native rebuild was not required.
